ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all founders, council members, protectors, and final beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Panama Superintendencia de Bancos risk lists (SIV); enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds verification for any PEP identification; continuous monitoring obligations under Ley 23 de 2015 and the Registro Público's beneficial ownership verification procedures.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Registro de Personas Jurídicas (online name clearance and reservation through the official Portal de Servicios en Línea of the Registro Público de Panamá, operated at www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names may be registered in Spanish or any language using the Latin alphabet; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet at the time of reservation. The name must be distinguishable from all existing registered entities and must include the identifying token 'Fundación' or its accepted abbreviation at the end of the full legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon an adverse name determination, the applicant, through the licensed resident agent, may file a written reconsideration (recurso de reconsideración) with the Dirección General de Registro del Registro Público de Panamá within five working days of notification, providing evidence of distinctiveness and prior use if applicable; if reconsideration is denied, a second hierarchical appeal (recurso de apelación) may be filed before the Director General within five working days; a new reservation request with a corrected denomination may be submitted immediately without prejudice. Judicial review is available through the Jurisdicción Contencioso-Administrativa de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within two months of final administrative denial.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible. A licensed Panamanian resident agent's registered address fully satisfies the statutory registered office mandate for a Private Interest Foundation. No physical office, staff, or local operations in Panama are required where the foundation acts purely as a holding vehicle for intellectual property and mobile application revenue. However, if the foundation were to engage in activities physically carried out in Panama, the economic substance rules under Ley 23 de 2015 and the OECD standard applicable to low-risk IP-holding arrangements would require review; the present app-store freemium business, executed entirely outside Panama through intermediaries, does not trigger local substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximately 10% probability of a formal on-site inspection during the first 36 months, focused primarily on the resident agent's physical premises and custody of foundation records rather than any foundation operational site; the low probability reflects the foundation's non-operational, asset-holding structure and the Low_Risk_Standard AML classification of mobile utility software under ISIC 6201.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley Nº 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as implemented by Executive Decree No. 36 of 12 July 1996; key provisions: Articles 1, 3, 5, 8, 12, 18, 19, and 25 (formation, initial patrimony, resident agent, Foundation Council, beneficiaries, and dissolution).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Dirección General de Registro, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Archivo de Ciudad de Panamá.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Fundación de Interés Privado Foundation Charter — Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (notarial Act of Foundation).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Law 25 of 1995, Article 8, requires the Charter to declare an initial patrimony of at least US$10,000.00 (or foreign-currency equivalent). No escrow deposit, bank certificate, or immediate contribution is required at registration; the amount is declared under oath by the Founder. Contributions in cash or in-kind may be made progressively pursuant to Foundation Council resolutions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL - DATED [DATE]

WHEREAS, the Private Interest Foundation (the 'Foundation') was constituted under Law 25 of 1995.

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED:

1. The Foundation Charter is ratified in full, including the initial patrimony declaration of US$10,000.
2. The registered office at [ADDRESS], Panama City, and resident agent [RESIDENT AGENT] are confirmed.
3. Officers appointed: [CHAIRPERSON], [SECRETARY], and [TREASURER], to serve until successors are appointed.
4. The Internal Regulations are adopted.
5. The officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute Apple and Google app-store agreements, and engage professional advisors.

ADOPTED by unanimous written consent of the Council, effective [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Online Entity Name Consultation Portal (Consulta en Línea de Personas Jurídicas)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two or three alternative names formatted as 'FOUNDATION NAME, Fundación de Interés Privado' through the Public Registry's online search module or via a licensed Panamanian attorney. Obtain the negative certificate (certificado de búsqueda de nombre) confirming that no identical or confusingly similar legal person is registered. Pay the search fee and retain the certificate for filing together with the Charter.
required_dossiers: Three proposed foundation names
Identity/passport copy of the Founder
Name-search fee receipt and official request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, select the next available alternative and resubmit the search. The rejection may be reconsidered by the Public Registry upon written request submitted within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de Panamá (Panamanian Notary Public) assisted by licensed counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct Panamanian counsel to draft the Foundation Charter under Law 25 of 1995, including the foundation name, mobile utility software development and app-store distribution purpose clause, initial asset declaration of US$10,000, duration, Foundation Council members, beneficiary or letter of wishes, resident agent clause, and amendment/dissolution rules. The Founder, Council members, and the attorney representing the resident agent must appear before the Notary to execute the deed and approve the notarial protocol.
required_dossiers: Name availability certificate
Passport copies of the Founder and Foundation Council members
Approved draft Foundation Charter
Resident agent acceptance letter and registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary's compliance department requests beneficial-owner documentation under Panamanian AML rules, file the Notary's standard KYC questionnaire and a lawful-origin of funds declaration; amend and re-sign the deed within the same protocol without loss of filing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Ciudad de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original first notarial copy (primer testimonio) of the executed Charter together with the name-search certificate, proof of payment of registration fees, and a cover letter requesting inscription as a Private Interest Foundation. The Registry assigns the foundation's file number (ficha) and issues the Certificate of Registration (certificado de inscripción). Filing may be completed physically at the Registry counter or electronically through authorized counsel.
required_dossiers: Notarized first copy of the Foundation Charter
Name-search certificate
Registration fee deposit receipt
Registry cover letter and power of attorney if filed via counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues observations (defectos), counsel must respond within 10 business days by filing explanatory briefs or a notarized corrective addendum (mutación) to the Charter; an uncured defect requires re-notarization and payment of an additional registration fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration - RUC and Annual Tax Standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) by submitting the DGI-01 application, a copy of the registered Charter, and identification of the Council members. Because Panama applies territorial taxation and the Foundation's app-store income (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing) is sourced from non-Panamanian users, such income is extraterritorial and not subject to Panamanian income tax; the RUC is maintained for banking, billing, and compliance purposes. Verify whether the annual unique legal-person fee applies to the Foundation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration from the Public Registry
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
Passport copies of the Foundation Council officers
DGI-01 registration form
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI questions the territorial-source treatment of app-store revenue, file a tax-law memorandum with the DGI and, if necessary, request a prior tax ruling (consulta tributaria) from the DGI Legal Directorate under the Fiscal Code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Agent and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Resident agent law firm registered with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the appointment of the resident agent (abogado idóneo) and the registered office in Panama City. The resident agent must hold the Foundation's statutory files, receive service of process, and maintain the Registry documents. Issue a Foundation Council minute confirming the agent's appointment and annual fee; the Registry certificate must reflect the registered address before any bank account is opened.
required_dossiers: Signed resident agent acceptance letter
Registered office address confirmation and occupancy title
Foundation Council minute confirming the agent's appointment
Receipt of the annual resident agent fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resident agent resigns or is removed, the Council must execute a notarized Charter amendment appointing a substitute agent and file it with the Public Registry within 30 days; otherwise the Registry may suspend the Foundation's good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Integration - Bank, App-Store, and Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian bank licensed by Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá; Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account for the Foundation using the registered Charter, RUC, Council minutes, and KYC documents. Complete Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console enrollment with the Foundation as the legal entity, executing the Apple iOS Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Distribution Agreement. Establish foundational records (asset register, minutes, resolutions) and register with the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) only if any activity is later deemed a non-financial regulated activity; otherwise maintain year-end records for audit readiness.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration and RUC certificate
Foundation Council minutes appointing officers
Passport copies and proof of address of officers and beneficiary
Banking reference letters
Apple D-U-N-S number application and Google Play developer account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or app-store platform requests enhanced due diligence (source of funds, structure chart), provide a notarized beneficial-ownership declaration and a legal opinion from Panamanian counsel explaining the Foundation's legitimate asset-holding purpose and the lawful source of the initial US$10,000 contribution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for digital software operations; reference authorities: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) and Municipality of Panama for any future physical office or municipal Aviso de Operación.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or commercial operating license is required for a Private Interest Foundation holding and licensing mobile utility software; if a future Panama operating company opens a physical branch, a municipal Aviso de Operación (Business Operation Notice) would apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III - Exempt: pure software/IP holding and digital distribution with zero physical industrial footprint; no EIA study required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - the Foundation has no wastewater, VOC, hazardous waste, or atmospheric emissions. Cloud hosting shall be provided by SOC 2 / ISO 27001-certified data centers, and user personal data shall be processed in accordance with Panama Law No. 81 of 2019 and applicable app-store privacy requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable while the Foundation maintains no physical premises. If an administrative office is later opened, obtain: (i) fire-safety inspection certificate from Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; (ii) structural occupancy clearance from the Municipality of Panama; and (iii) workplace health and safety registration with Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; online portal: SISTEMA T@X-ON (https://tatonline.mef.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) engaged in mobile utility app sales in Panama: 1. Obtain the foundation's registered agent and resident representative in Panama. 2. Draft and notarize the foundation charter (Acta Constitutiva) and register with the Public Registry of Panama. 3. Apply for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) at the DGI through the T@X-ON system or in person, submitting the registered charter excerpt (testimonio), registered agent details, identity documents of the foundation council members, and proof of the foundation's local address. 4. Obtain a Notice of Operation (Aviso de Operación) if the foundation will carry out taxable activities in Panama, or file as a non-resident digital services provider if applicable. 5. Receive the RUC number and digital tax certificate, then enable T@X-ON access for filing declarations and electronic invoicing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama applies a territorial tax system for PIFs; foreign-source income derived from outside Panama is not subject to Panama income tax and no check-the-box election is offered in the U.S. sense. A PIF operating through Panama-resident activities (e.g., executing app sales through a Panama branch or receiving Panamanian-source revenue) is subject to entity-level corporate income tax at a flat 25% under the territorial regime, unless it qualifies as a small business (15%) or as a Multinational Headquarters (SEM) enterprise with alternative tax rules. A PIF may elect to be treated as a foundation with a segregated patrimony (estate) rather than a corporation, but no U.S.-style hybrid entity classification election is available. For withholding tax and FATCA/CRS purposes, a PIF is generally classified as a financial institution if it is an investment entity, or as a passive NFFE if primarily engaged in commercial digital app sales.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Corporales Muebles y la Prestación de Servicios (ITBMS - VAT/GST equivalent)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Taxable persons are required to register for ITBMS once they engage in taxable activities; the DGI imposes no universal numeric turnover threshold for non-resident digital suppliers other than the general obligation of any person carrying out taxable acts in Panama. To be considered a taxable person for ITBMS, a foreign supplier is required to register from the first sale when the customer is a Panama-resident consumer or when the digital platform is marketed to Panama users. For local entities, voluntary registration is permitted. There is no small-supplier exemption of general application above zero for digital B2C services after the 2016 reform.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has made electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) mandatory under the DGI 'Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá (SFEP)' since 2021, phased-in between 2021 and 2024. The T@X-ON platform enables the issuance of e-invoices with QR codes and digital stamps. Real-time clearance is required for generally regulated taxpayers in categories established by DGI Resolution 202-2021; the DGI requires online validation through the SFEP for most e-invoices, with the generation of a unique CUF (Código Único de Facturación) digital signature for each transaction. Payment gateways (Apple/Google) are treated as intermediaries; the Panamanian ITBMS registration must use the DGI's simplified regime for foreign digital service suppliers. Data retention of all e-invoice records is six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods from Panama qualifies for ITBMS zero-rating when the seller proves the goods are physically transferred to a foreign destination. Export of services or digital products is zero-rated only when the service is effectively used or exploited in a foreign territory and the recipient is not a Panama resident; the payer must be domiciled abroad and the benefit or use must occur outside Panama. For a mobile utility app downloaded via Apple/Google app stores by foreign users, the supply is considered an export of services if the economic exploitation/performance is abroad, but the DGI may require that the Panamanian entity maintains evidence that the service was not used within Panama. Software delivered by download from a foreign platform to a Panamanian user is subject to ITBMS at 7%, and the platform remits through the VAT/simplified regime. Offshore services to multinational clients outside Panama are zero-rated if all the preconditions of Article 186(f) of the Panamanian Fiscal Code (export of services) are satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación de Mercancías) via SICARGA/SIGA Panama Customs
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (knowledge of lading covering physical export movement)
Proof of Foreign Payment / Inward Remittance Certificate from a Panama licensed bank (Certificado de Liquidación de Divisas / comprobante de ingreso de divisas)
Copy of the digital service contract or end-user consumption report from the app store platform
ITBMS Export Ledger and statutory export register (Registro de Exportaciones)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unjustified export zero-rating claims by a PIF are subject to the DGI's general corrective assessment regime, with a statute of limitations of 5 years (rising to 7 years for omissions). The ITBMS under-declaration penalty is 50-100% of the evaded tax. Interest accrues at the applicable DGI rate (currently 10% per annum plus 1% monthly surcharge). The DGI may also impose fines under the Procedural Code for non-compliance with e-invoicing requirements, which range from USD 500 to USD 50,000 per invoicing irregularity, and for failure to issue validated e-invoices. Where a PIF is used to artificially claim zero-rating without substantive foreign export or with sham foreign recipients, the government may retroactively disallow the zero-rating and obtain an automatic prior lien for all unpaid taxes, and tax evasion sanctions under Panamanian Criminal Law apply where the fraudulent amount exceeds USD 10,000, carrying imprisonment and monetary penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank and no foreign-exchange administration. Banking supervision is exercised exclusively by the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, SBP) under Legislative Decree No. 2 of 2008. AML/CFT supervision is performed by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) under Law No. 23 of 2015.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The US Dollar (USD) is legal tender in parallel with the Balboa (PAB) at a fixed 1:1 parity, producing complete de facto dollarization. There is no capital-account or current-account exchange-control regime and no license, registration, or prior-approval requirement for foreign-currency transactions. Profit remittances, beneficiary distributions, and cross-border movement of app-store royalties are unrestricted and are subject only to transactional due diligence by the receiving bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Because USD is national legal tender, Panama imposes no export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio, no repatriation timeline, and no clearing through a central account. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlements may remain in USD indefinitely without reporting to the SBP.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account in USD (initial endowment)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Panama does not issue standalone electronic money institution (EMI) licenses; payment service providers require a banking license or admission to the SBP regulatory sandbox established under the digital-economy framework (Law No. 166 of 2020). Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, or Payoneer cannot serve as the PIF's primary settlement account because Apple and Google require the receiving account to be titled in the exact legal name of the developer with full SWIFT metadata. The recommended architecture is a Tier-1 domestic bank account for all app-store settlements, with an optional EMI used only for small-value cross-border contractor disbursements if the EMI accepts Panama-domiciled foundations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is lawful when the PIF presents a notarized foundation charter, a notarized power of attorney, and a legal-opinion letter from a licensed Panamanian attorney. In practice, Banco General and Global Bank will accept an attorney-vouched dossier with a live video interview of the beneficial owner; Banco Nacional de Panamá and Banistmo generally require physical presence of at least one foundation council member or of the appointed local attorney holding the registered power of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation charter invokes statutory beneficiary confidentiality, conflicting with Law 23 of 2015 beneficial-ownership disclosure duties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter (Pacto Fundacional) and statutes; confidential council-member list filed with the Public Registry of Panama; foundation-council resolution expressly authorizing disclosure to the bank; signed beneficial-ownership declaration; valid passports and source-of-funds evidence for all council members and beneficiaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF appears as a shell with no commercial activity or economic substance, triggering structuring-red-flag scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console developer agreements identifying the PIF as developer of record; board minutes authorizing the freemium mobile utility activity; revenue and disbursement projections; economic-substance declaration filed with the Dirección General de Ingresos under Executive Decree No. 120 of 2019 confirming adequate real activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Irregular inbound lump-sum settlements from Apple and Google distribution entities inconsistent with declared monthly app revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple and Google monthly payout statements with transaction identifiers; developer-console settlement and tax-documentation pages; treasury reconciliation memorandum mapping each remittance to platform settlement reports; signed auditor or accountant confirmation of revenue apportionment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No locally resident responsible person, with all foundation council members resident in foreign jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized special power of attorney granted to a Panamanian attorney or resident council member; certificate of appointment and acceptance; professional curricula vitae; bank and professional references covering the past 12 months; physical address certificate for the foundation's registered office in Panama.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Founder endowment is credited by SWIFT MT103 from the founder's bank to the PIF capital escrow account at Global Bank with payment reference 'CUST-PIF endowment contribution' and citation of the foundation charter; no Panamanian prior approval is required. Operating proceeds are remitted in USD by Apple (typically Apple Distribution International Ltd.) and Google (typically Google Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd. or Google Ireland Ltd.) via SWIFT MT103 or ACH to the PIF's domestic account within 45 days after the close of the App Store sales month and within approximately 15 days after the Google Play payout cycle; the settlement account must match the developer-account legal name exactly. Funds clear in USD with zero conversion because the Balboa is pegged 1:1 to the dollar; verification is achieved by reconciling developer-console payout statements with incoming bank credits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Contractor and vendor disbursements are executed via SWIFT MT103 for foreign beneficiaries and through the SBP-supervised national automated clearing house for domestic USD credits. Procurement of cloud infrastructure, advertising inventory, or hardware above USD 250,000 should be supported by an irrevocable commercial letter of credit opened at Banco General and advised through the vendor's correspondent bank. Every outbound message must reference the underlying app-store transaction or invoice number to preserve an auditable trail for UAF examinations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards: permitted with Panamanian banks to lock EUR or GBP conversion of app-store receipts into USD; no hedge is required for local Balboa exposure because USD is legal tender.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): available through banks licensed under Legislative Decree No. 2 of 2008 for emerging-market currencies (Latin America and Asia), subject to evidence of a real underlying trade-flow exposure from digital downloads.

Cross-Currency Swaps: permissible for balance-sheet hedging of multi-currency contractor or licensing agreements exceeding USD 1 million, executed via the international desk of Banco General or Global Bank.
USD Call Options: not prohibited, but sourced through an international securities broker and settled via the PIF's brokerage account rather than a bank retail platform.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Franchise Tax (Tasa Anual de las Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) via the Treasury Collection Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and March 31; payment by January 31 avoids late surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: USD 50 surcharge if paid in February and USD 100 if paid in March; from April 1 the foundation is declared 'en mora', loses good standing and access to Paz y Salvo certificates and stamped registry documents; prolonged non-payment triggers administrative strike-off and cancellation by the Public Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Sworn Ultimate Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Special Beneficial Ownership System), with DGI data verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing within 30 days of registration; annual renewal due within 120 days after the close of the fiscal year (by April 30 for calendar-year foundations); supplementary update within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership or foundation council membership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines between USD 1,000 and USD 10,000 imposed on the foundation, foundation council members, and resident agent under Law 129 of 2020; registry amendments blocked until the declaration is regularized; false or omitted UBO data carries criminal liability and may trigger administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Formulario 10) — conditional on Panamanian-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by March 31 of the following calendar year if the PIF derives taxable income from Panamanian source; no filing obligation for a non-resident PIF earning exclusively foreign-source mobile app store revenue through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine of 25% of the tax due, plus monthly interest on the unpaid tax and inflation-indexed surcharges; persistent non-filing results in DGI tax lien certification, suspension of good-standing certificates, and restriction on registry transactions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Business License Renewal (Patente Municipal / Aviso de Operación) — conditional on physical local operation in Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipality of the operating district and DGI Aviso de Operación system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal effective January 1 of each calendar year; not applicable to a non-resident PIF that sells mobile software solely through digital app stores and maintains no Panama place of business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment interest of 1%, municipal closure orders for unlicensed physical premises, disqualification from municipal procurement, and potential cancellation of the local operating permit

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995; an independent certified audit is triggered only if the foundation generates Panamanian-source gross income of at least USD 3,000,000 or holds total assets of at least USD 7,000,000 under Executive Decree No. 91 of 2018, or when the foundation charter mandates one
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama (NIIF), with IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para PYMES) permitted for small and micro entities; a non-resident PIF without Panamanian-source income is not required to prepare or file audited financial statements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent maintains the private UBO register and annually re-files the sworn beneficial owner declaration with the Public Registry within 120 days of fiscal year-end; any transfer of foundation beneficiary interests, change of beneficiaries, or replacement of foundation council members must be minuted and notified to the resident agent within 30 days so the declaration is updated before the next annual confirmation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 to USD 1,200 per year for resident agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for a dormant non-resident PIF; USD 2,500 to USD 6,500 only if the USD 3,000,000 Panama-source gross income audit threshold is exceeded
